usageNotes: Use this as a discovery entry point to enumerate all top-level cluster API namespaces (e.g. config, ha, log, resources, tasks). It requires no parameters and is accessible to any authenticated user or API token, making it a safe first call for capability probing. The response is an array of child resource descriptors, not cluster status data — use get_cluster_resources for live node/VM/storage state.

examples.summary: List all top-level cluster API namespaces

tips: The 'name' field in each returned object matches the href link relation and can be appended to /cluster/ to form the child endpoint path.
This endpoint returns structural metadata only — it does not reflect cluster health or membership. Use get_cluster_status for that.
Works on standalone (non-clustered) PVE nodes as well; the child namespaces returned are the same regardless of cluster membership.
